mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 5% simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth recovers above 2% within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or inflation remains below 2% during the period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the contraction reverses within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or inflation falls below 3% within the period.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both real personal income (proxied by RSAFS) and the housing starts index (HOUST) above their 12-month moving averages signals strengthening household demand, which boosts consumption and investment, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or either proxy reverts below its moving average within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or PAYEMS growth decelerates below 0.2% month-over-month within the period.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between the trajectory of real GDP (GDPC1) and S&P 500 forward returns at the 5-day horizon; rising GDP growth expectations (quarter-over-quarter change in GDPC1 above 2%) predict positive short-term equity returns.
failure_condition: The correlation between GDPC1 qoq change and 5-day S&P 500 returns falls below 0.3, or positive GDPC1 signals result in negative returns in more than 60% of cases.
